newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi refiners operating normally despite spill.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi refiners operating normally despite spill.

text.p: Operations of two Mitsubishi group refineries that were meant to accept crude oil from the Diamond Grace, which scrapped a reef in Tokyo Bay and leaked oil on Wednesday, are expected to remain unaffected by the accident, company officials said on Thursday.

The supertanker carrying 257,000 tonnes of crude oil from the United Arab Emirates was on its way to Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd's Kawasaki plant near Tokyo and Tohoku Oil Co Ltd's Sendai plant in northern Japan at the time of the accident.
The vessel was estimated to have spilled some 15,000 tonnes of its cargo into the bay.
"We don't expect to have a crude shortage as the offloading from the troubled tanker started early this morning," a Mitsubishi Oil spokesman said.
Production at the 75,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery has not been disrupted by the accident, the spokesman added.

Meanwhile, Tohoku Oil's Sendai plant on the Pacific coast, which has a crude processing capacity of 120,000 bpd, has been closed since late May for routine maintenance checks, a company spokesman said.
He also said there is enough time to figure out how to secure backup crude cargoes as the plant is scheduled to remain closed until mid-July.
